points.why: It separates potholes, which don't react to repairs, from homelessness, whose flows react to policy, but never says homelessness has a disputed definition or no natural stopping point.
It treats the four claims as different interacting flows with no single answer and warns that one program tests only one theory.

It raises the regional boundary and suggests learning pilots, but it never involves people experiencing homelessness, providers or neighboring cities, and it relies on data rather than drawing out views.
It explicitly keeps the headline count as one of several measures rather than the definition of the problem.

pitfalls.why: It rejects the pothole model and argues against funding a single cause.

notes: It claims local data will 'settle much of the committee argument with facts', which overstates how far data can resolve a problem whose framing is contested.
